sourcedFrom: Colt AR-15 Semiautomatic Rifles and Carbines Safety and Instruction Manual — Colt AR-15 Semiautomatic Rifles and Carbines (1995)
cleanIntro: Colt's own stripping procedure for its AR-15 semiautomatic carbines, then the cleaning it calls for. The book publishes two levels — the strip that opens the rifle, and a component disassembly of the bolt and buffer beyond it — so the Deep Clean here is entirely the manufacturer's.

steps.title: Selector to SAFE, magazine out
steps.action: Set the selector lever to SAFE, then press the magazine catch and remove the magazine. Keep the muzzle in a safe direction, your finger off the trigger and your hands away from the ejection port.
steps.prose: Selector first. On an AR the selector can only be set to SAFE with the hammer cocked, which is exactly the state the rifle is in until you have cleared it.
steps.quote: Press magazine catch and remove magazine.
steps.cite: Colt AR-15 Semiautomatic Rifles and Carbines Safety and Instruction Manual — Colt AR-15 Semiautomatic Rifles and Carbines — UNLOADING — To Unload, step 3, p.39
steps.warn: KEEP YOUR FIREARM POINTING IN A SAFE DIRECTION. DO NOT TOUCH TRIGGER AND KEEP HANDS AWAY FROM EJECTION PORT.

steps.title: Charging handle back, bolt held open
steps.action: Pull the charging handle to the rear and push in the lower portion of the bolt catch to hold the bolt open. Any round in the chamber should have been ejected as the bolt came back.
steps.prose: If the last round had been fired with the magazine in place, the bolt is already held to the rear. Do it anyway — the point is that you saw it happen.
steps.caution: If a round had been in the chamber it should have been ejected.
steps.quote: Pull charging handle to rear and push in lower portion of bolt catch.
steps.cite: Colt AR-15 Semiautomatic Rifles and Carbines Safety and Instruction Manual — Colt AR-15 Semiautomatic Rifles and Carbines — UNLOADING — To Unload, step 4, p.39

steps.title: Look into the chamber through the ejection port
steps.action: Look into the chamber through the ejection port to be certain it is empty.
steps.prose: Colt prints this one in capitals. Look at the chamber itself, not at the magazine well and not at the bolt face.
steps.quote: LOOK INTO CHAMBER THROUGH EJECTION PORT TO ENSURE CHAMBER IS EMPTY.
steps.cite: Colt AR-15 Semiautomatic Rifles and Carbines Safety and Instruction Manual — Colt AR-15 Semiautomatic Rifles and Carbines — UNLOADING — To Unload, step 5, p.39

steps.title: Empty the magazine and put the ammunition away
steps.action: Slide the remaining live rounds forward out of the magazine, then collect live ammunition for safe storage and spent cases for disposal before starting work.
steps.prose: Ammunition off the bench entirely. A stripped rifle and a loose round in the same place is how the worst accidents start.
steps.quote: Collect live ammunition for safe storage and spent cartridge cases for disposal.
steps.cite: Colt AR-15 Semiautomatic Rifles and Carbines Safety and Instruction Manual — Colt AR-15 Semiautomatic Rifles and Carbines — UNLOADING — To Unload, step 8, p.39

steps.title: Magazine out, rifle proven empty, parts laid out
steps.action: Confirm again that the magazine is removed and the firearm is not loaded, and lay the small components out in an orderly fashion as they come off so none is lost.
steps.prose: An AR sheds small pins and a cam pin that all look alike on a cluttered bench. Colt asks for order for a practical reason, not a tidy one.
steps.quote: lay them out in an orderly fashion.
steps.cite: Colt AR-15 Semiautomatic Rifles and Carbines Safety and Instruction Manual — Colt AR-15 Semiautomatic Rifles and Carbines — STRIPPING FOR CLEANING — IMPORTANT, p.45
steps.warn: WEAR SAFETY GLASSES IN CASE YOU LOSE CONTROL OF SOME SPRING LOADED COMPONENT WHICH COULD INJURE YOUR EYES.

steps.title: Push the takedown pin out to its stop
steps.action: Press the takedown pin in from the left of the lower receiver and pull the pin out on the right until it comes to a positive stop.
steps.prose: It is captive — it stops rather than coming free, and that stop is the correct position. Some models carry a flexible wedge behind the takedown pin that makes the receivers a tighter fit; that is normal, and a pin punch helps.
steps.quote: Press take down pin in from left of lower receiver and pull pin out on right of receiver until it comes to a positive stop.
steps.cite: Colt AR-15 Semiautomatic Rifles and Carbines Safety and Instruction Manual — Colt AR-15 Semiautomatic Rifles and Carbines — STRIPPING FOR CLEANING, step 2, p.45

steps.title: Pivot the lower away from the upper
steps.action: Pivot the lower receiver down and away from the upper receiver on the front pivot pin.
steps.prose: That alone opens the rifle enough to get the bolt carrier out, which is why most cleaning stops here.
steps.quote: Pivot lower receiver down and away from upper receiver.
steps.cite: Colt AR-15 Semiautomatic Rifles and Carbines Safety and Instruction Manual — Colt AR-15 Semiautomatic Rifles and Carbines — STRIPPING FOR CLEANING, step 3, p.45

steps.title: Separate the receivers if you want them apart
steps.action: For more convenience you may remove the pivot screw from the front of the receivers and separate them completely.
steps.prose: Colt marks this as optional, and it is. Two halves are easier to handle over a sink; one hinged unit is harder to lose.
steps.quote: If required for more convenience, remove pivot screw from front of receivers, and completely separate receivers.
steps.cite: Colt AR-15 Semiautomatic Rifles and Carbines Safety and Instruction Manual — Colt AR-15 Semiautomatic Rifles and Carbines — STRIPPING FOR CLEANING, step 4, p.46

steps.title: Bolt carrier assembly out
steps.action: Pull the charging handle to the rear and remove the bolt carrier assembly from the upper receiver.
steps.prose: The carrier rides out on the charging handle for the first inch or so, then lifts clear. Do not try to pull it out before the handle has moved.
steps.quote: Pull charging handle to rear and remove bolt carrier assembly
steps.cite: Colt AR-15 Semiautomatic Rifles and Carbines Safety and Instruction Manual — Colt AR-15 Semiautomatic Rifles and Carbines — STRIPPING FOR CLEANING, step 5, p.46

steps.title: Charging handle back to its keyway and down
steps.action: Remove the charging handle by pulling it backwards to the keyway and down out of the upper receiver.
steps.prose: Back to the keyway, then down. It will not come out anywhere else along its travel, and levering it will bend the latch.
steps.quote: Remove charging handle by pulling it backwards
steps.cite: Colt AR-15 Semiautomatic Rifles and Carbines Safety and Instruction Manual — Colt AR-15 Semiautomatic Rifles and Carbines — STRIPPING FOR CLEANING, step 6, p.46

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: Upper receiver with barrel, lower receiver, bolt carrier assembly, charging handle and magazine. That is enough to clean the rifle; everything past it is component disassembly, which Colt also publishes.
steps.prose: Reassembly is the same list backwards, and Colt says so — steps 15 through 1, with one thing that must be checked at the end.
steps.caution: CAUTION: IF YOU ATTEMPT TO FIRE WITHOUT THE CAM PIN INSTALLED, DAMAGE OR INJURY MAY RESULT.
steps.quote: Reassemble your firearm by reversing the stripping procedure already described
steps.cite: Colt AR-15 Semiautomatic Rifles and Carbines Safety and Instruction Manual — Colt AR-15 Semiautomatic Rifles and Carbines — STRIPPING FOR CLEANING — IMPORTANT, p.52

deepSteps.title: Firing pin retaining pin out to the left
deepSteps.action: Push the firing pin retaining pin in from the right side of the bolt carrier and pull it out to the left.
deepSteps.prose: Right to left, and out to the left. It is a small split pin — push it, do not drive it.
deepSteps.quote: Push in firing pin retaining pin from right to left of bolt carrier
deepSteps.cite: Colt AR-15 Semiautomatic Rifles and Carbines Safety and Instruction Manual — Colt AR-15 Semiautomatic Rifles and Carbines — STRIPPING FOR CLEANING, step 7, p.49

deepSteps.title: Tilt the bolt face up and drop the firing pin out
deepSteps.action: Tilt the carrier bolt-face-up and remove the firing pin. On a .223 carbine there is no firing pin spring; the 9mm carbine has one and it comes out with the pin.
deepSteps.prose: Gravity does it. If the firing pin will not fall, the retaining pin is not fully clear.
deepSteps.quote: Tilt bolt face up and remove firing pin from the 223 Carbine
deepSteps.cite: Colt AR-15 Semiautomatic Rifles and Carbines Safety and Instruction Manual — Colt AR-15 Semiautomatic Rifles and Carbines — STRIPPING FOR CLEANING, step 8, p.49

deepSteps.title: The next four steps are .223 only
deepSteps.action: Before going on, note the boundary Colt draws on this page: steps 9 through 12 — cam pin, bolt out of the carrier, extractor — apply to .223 calibre carbines and do NOT apply to the 9mm carbine, which has a different bolt.
deepSteps.prose: Two procedures share this page. Reading straight down it is how a 9mm bolt gets treated as a .223 one, so read the note before the step.
deepSteps.quote: and do NOT apply to the 9mm Carbine.
deepSteps.cite: Colt AR-15 Semiautomatic Rifles and Carbines Safety and Instruction Manual — Colt AR-15 Semiautomatic Rifles and Carbines — STRIPPING FOR CLEANING, note before step 9, p.49

deepSteps.title: Push the bolt in and turn the cam pin a quarter turn
deepSteps.action: Push the bolt in towards the carrier until it rotates and comes to a stop, then turn the bolt cam pin through 90 degrees — at right angles to its normal position.
deepSteps.prose: The bolt has to be pushed in first or the cam pin is trapped by the carrier key. Turning it a quarter turn is what lines it up to lift.
deepSteps.quote: Push bolt in towards the carrier until bolt rotates and comes to a stop, then turn bolt cam pin through
deepSteps.cite: Colt AR-15 Semiautomatic Rifles and Carbines Safety and Instruction Manual — Colt AR-15 Semiautomatic Rifles and Carbines — STRIPPING FOR CLEANING, step 9, p.49

deepSteps.title: Lift the cam pin out, then draw the bolt forward
deepSteps.action: Lift the cam pin out away from the bolt and bolt carrier, then pull the bolt forward out of the carrier.
deepSteps.prose: The cam pin is the one part on this rifle whose absence is catastrophic and invisible once the carrier is back together — put it where you will see it.
deepSteps.caution: CAUTION: IF YOU ATTEMPT TO FIRE WITHOUT THE CAM PIN INSTALLED, DAMAGE OR INJURY MAY RESULT.
deepSteps.quote: Remove cam pin by lifting it out away
deepSteps.cite: Colt AR-15 Semiautomatic Rifles and Carbines Safety and Instruction Manual — Colt AR-15 Semiautomatic Rifles and Carbines — STRIPPING FOR CLEANING, steps 10 and 11, p.49

deepSteps.title: Never touch the ejector retaining pin
deepSteps.action: The bolt carries two small pins near its front. Only the extractor pin comes out. Do not attempt to remove the ejector retaining pin, which is the smaller one and sits nearer the front of the bolt.
deepSteps.prose: The ejector is under a strong spring in a blind hole, and it is the part that turns a cleaning session into a parts order. Colt names it specifically so it cannot be mistaken for the extractor pin.
deepSteps.quote: Do not attempt to remove the ejector retaining pin which is smaller and nearer the front of the bolt.
deepSteps.cite: Colt AR-15 Semiautomatic Rifles and Carbines Safety and Instruction Manual — Colt AR-15 Semiautomatic Rifles and Carbines — STRIPPING FOR CLEANING — IMPORTANT, before step 12, p.49

deepSteps.title: Extractor pin out, controlling the extractor spring
deepSteps.action: Be ready to stop the extractor spring moving before the pin comes out, then press the extractor pin in on the right of the bolt, pull it out on the left, and lift the extractor off.
deepSteps.prose: The spring sits under the extractor with a rubber insert inside it. Thumb over the extractor as the pin leaves, and it stays where you put it.
deepSteps.quote: IMPORTANT: Before removing extractor pin, be prepared to prevent movement of extractor spring.
deepSteps.cite: Colt AR-15 Semiautomatic Rifles and Carbines Safety and Instruction Manual — Colt AR-15 Semiautomatic Rifles and Carbines — STRIPPING FOR CLEANING, step 12, p.49

deepSteps.title: Handguards off, only if they need it
deepSteps.action: Pull back on the handguard slip-ring until it is clear of both handguard sections and remove them. Colt marks this as unnecessary unless dirt has accumulated in or around the handguards.
deepSteps.prose: The slip-ring is stiff by design and the two halves come off together. If nothing has got in behind them, leave them alone.
deepSteps.quote: Note: This item is not necessary unless dirt has accumulated in or around the handguards.
deepSteps.cite: Colt AR-15 Semiautomatic Rifles and Carbines Safety and Instruction Manual — Colt AR-15 Semiautomatic Rifles and Carbines — STRIPPING FOR CLEANING, step 13, p.50

deepSteps.title: Buttstock off the receiver extension
deepSteps.action: Push the release lever up and extend the buttstock fully, then push the lever down and pull the buttstock rearward off the receiver extension.
deepSteps.prose: Up, out, down, off. That order matters on a collapsible stock — pulling before the lever is down just jams it on a detent.
deepSteps.quote: Remove buttstock from lower receiver: first push release lever up and extend buttstock fully, then push lever down and pull buttstock rearward.
deepSteps.cite: Colt AR-15 Semiautomatic Rifles and Carbines Safety and Instruction Manual — Colt AR-15 Semiautomatic Rifles and Carbines — STRIPPING FOR CLEANING, step 14, p.51

deepSteps.title: Buffer and action spring out under control
deepSteps.action: Depress the buffer and keep pressure on it — it is under spring tension and will be ejected the moment the buffer retainer is depressed. Depress the buffer retainer to let buffer and action spring move forward, then depress the hammer so they can travel fully out of the receiver extension.
deepSteps.prose: The buffer leaves the tube like a small cannon if you let go. The hammer has to be pushed down or the buffer will not clear it.
deepSteps.quote: Depress buffer, maintaining pressure as buffer is under spring tension, to prevent it from being ejected when buffer retainer is depressed.
deepSteps.cite: Colt AR-15 Semiautomatic Rifles and Carbines Safety and Instruction Manual — Colt AR-15 Semiautomatic Rifles and Carbines — STRIPPING FOR CLEANING, step 15, p.51
deepSteps.warn: Wear safety glasses — this is the spring-loaded component the manual's caution is about.

deepSteps.title: That is the end of the disassembly Colt publishes
deepSteps.action: Fifteen steps and no more. Colt states not to strip the firearm further than described, and directs anything beyond it to Service and Repair. Reassemble by reversing steps 15 through 1, and be certain the cam pin is properly installed.
deepSteps.prose: The cam pin gets its own sentence at the end because a carrier will go back together without it and the rifle will not survive being fired that way.
deepSteps.quote: Do not strip your firearm further than previously described.
deepSteps.cite: Colt AR-15 Semiautomatic Rifles and Carbines Safety and Instruction Manual — Colt AR-15 Semiautomatic Rifles and Carbines — STRIPPING FOR CLEANING — IMPORTANT, p.52
deepSteps.warn: CAUTION: IF YOU ATTEMPT TO FIRE WITHOUT THE CAM PIN INSTALLED, DAMAGE OR INJURY MAY RESULT.

cleaning.name: BARREL AND CHAMBER
tasks: Attach a cotton flannel patch to the cleaning rod, insert it in the chamber and pass rod and patch down through the barrel, changing patches with each pass until the last comes out clean
Inspect the bore; if it is still dirty after firing, run a brass wire bristle brush wet with gun cleaning solution the full length before reversing direction
Clean the chamber with the larger chamber brush: a minimum of five plunge strokes and three full clockwise rotational strokes
Avoid contact between the cleaning rod and the muzzle — that wear reduces accuracy
Before firing, check that barrel and chamber are clean and dry

cleaning.name: BOLT, CARRIER AND GAS TUBE
tasks: Using the bore brush still wet with cleaning solution, clean carbon and powder residue from around the gas tube in the upper receiver, the bolt locking lugs, the bolt rings, the firing pin, the bolt cam pin, the lip of the extractor, and inside the bolt carrier from both front and rear
Wipe all components clean and dry and inspect them for excessive wear, corrosion or mechanical damage — if any is found, have it corrected before firing again
Do not use a wire brush on aluminium surfaces such as the receivers; use a small toothbrush or flannel patch instead

cleaning.name: LUBRICATION POINTS
tasks: Lightly moisten a flannel patch with gun oil and pass it once through the barrel, leaving a thin film — pass a dry patch through instead if the rifle is going back into use rather than storage

Lightly lubricate the windage drum and rear sight detents, the ejection port cover latch and spring, the action springs and pins, the front sight detent, the charging handle catch and its spring, inside the rear of the bolt, the mouth of the bolt key, the bolt carrier exhaust ports and the forward assist
Below freezing, avoid oil and apply a dry lubricant sparingly instead
After reassembly, remove gun cleaning solution, oil and fingerprints from the outside surfaces

cleaning.name: MAGAZINE
tasks: Clean the magazine whenever the firearm is cleaned
With the magazine empty, remove the bottom plate by pressing in on the spring catch beneath the small round hole and sliding the plate off while controlling the spring
Remove the five-round spacer if one is fitted, let the spring extend, then remove spring and follower — it can and should be done without force
Clean all components, wipe the spring with a light coat of oil, leave everything else dry and reassemble in reverse
If a magazine is difficult to disassemble, clean it as best you can assembled rather than risk damaging it

cleaning.name: HOW OFTEN
tasks: After firing, clean as soon as possible, then check it again within a few days to be sure no further cleaning is needed
Unfired, clean it at least once or twice a year in a temperate climate, or as often as once a week in a tropical one
If you keep it loaded, unload and clean it at least once a month; if it gets wet, clean it as soon as possible

reassembly: Reassemble by reversing the stripping procedure — steps 15 through 1 — and be certain the cam pin is properly installed.
Extractor and its spring back into the bolt, extractor pin in from the left; bolt into the carrier, cam pin down through the carrier and turned back to its normal position.
Firing pin in from the rear, then the firing pin retaining pin in from the left — check the firing pin cannot fall out before going further.
Action spring and buffer into the receiver extension until the buffer retainer catches the buffer; buttstock back on and the release lever seated.
Handguards on, slip-ring pulled back and released to capture both halves.
Charging handle into its keyway and forward, bolt carrier assembly in behind it, receivers closed and the takedown pin pushed home.

Some models carry a flexible wedge in the rear of the lower receiver to make the union tighter — closing the receivers takes more effort on those, which is normal; use a pin punch on the takedown pin if needed.
fncheck: With the magazine out and the chamber checked empty, set the selector to SAFE and confirm the trigger will not release the hammer, then to FIRE and confirm it will, easing the hammer down under thumb control. Work the charging handle and confirm the bolt goes fully into battery and the bolt catch holds it open. Above all, confirm the cam pin is installed — Colt warns that firing without it may cause damage or injury.
